question: What do the checksums of a frame and of a segment cost a command, and what is left of it when they are taken eight bytes at a step?
method: The CRC-16 of the AC-3 family and the CRC-8 of a TrueHD substream segment went through a byte table a byte at a time. They keep eight tables and take eight bytes at a step. The kernels of the two were timed before and after, bound to the fast cores (`tools/kernels.py --affinity FFFF --runs 5`). What the change is worth to a command was measured inside one binary, built for the purpose with a switch that sends the checksums through the bytes one at a time: both ways turn and turn about, nine runs each, bound to the fast cores, so that the two differ by the change and by nothing else. The binary of the change was also measured against the binary of main in the usual way (`tools/bench.py --compare`, five runs), and the one stream that came out slower there was looked into: on fixed processors, with variants of the build, with timers around the stages of the decoder, and in the one binary. That nothing a command says or writes changed was looked for over the corpus (`tools/old_new.py --decode-all`) and in the campaign of evidence 22. The streams are media and are not in the repository.

kernels.kernel: eac3: decode the 5.1 core of the object stream
joc: analysis bank, one channel, one frame
joc: synthesis bank, one object, one frame

the_change_inside_one_binary.how: one binary with a switch in its environment; the time of a command with the checksums eight bytes at a step over its time with them a byte at a time, medians of nine runs each

decode_of_its_widest_presentation_on_fix.how: eleven runs each, the two binaries turn and turn about; `over_the_first` is over main
decode_of_its_widest_presentation_on_fix.reading: on one logical processor the two threads of the command share it and the time is the sum of their work: the check of the stream beside the decode costs less with the change, and the sum does not go down, so the thread that decodes does more

variants_of_the_build.how: the same command, bound to the fast cores, eleven runs each
variants_of_the_build.reading: every build in which the CRC-8 goes eight bytes at a step is the slower one, whether the routine is in line or not and whether its tables are constants or statics

the_stages_in_a_build_with_timers.how: timers around the stages in a throwaway build, once with the checksums of main and once with the change; the least of five runs. The timers cost time, and they move the code
the_stages_in_a_build_with_timers.reading: the matrix stage is the same source in both builds and differs by more than the checks of all the segments cost, here in favour of the build with the change

the_stream_that_came_out_slower.reading: The checksums of this stream are faster with the change like those of every other, and the same presentation decodes in less time when one binary takes them eight bytes at a step. What is slower in the binary of the change is the rest of the thread that decodes, most of which is the matrix stage: the compiler built or placed it otherwise in this build, and it is slower for this stream and not for the others. It is the stream that asks most of that stage (`what_the_matrix_stage_multiplies`). What about the matrix loop is so easily moved was not found.

what_the_matrix_stage_multiplies.how: counters in a throwaway build, over the decode of the widest presentation of the two 16-channel streams of the comparison

a_run_over_the_corpus_before_and_after.reading: the checksums of these streams were written by other encoders: the streams that were sound are sound and the ten that were not are not

reading: A megabyte of CRC-16 takes 0.38 ms where it took 1.81, and of CRC-8 0.31 where it took 1.33. Inside one binary, `verify` takes 88.8 to 97.0 per cent of the time and the widest decode 92.4 to 97.8, on eight streams of both families and every one of sixteen measurements faster. Between the binary of main and the binary of the change, 65 of 88 commands are faster and 3 slower, the three of one stream, where the matrix stage of the widest presentation came out of the compiler slower in this build. A difference of a few per cent between two binaries is not a measurement of a change of the source.
